The ONE outlier, on#1, differs from ALL THREE OTHERS, including the OTHER 'on' run (on#2). Two runs sharing the SAME instrument state (on#1 vs on#2) disagreeing with EACH OTHER is direct, positive proof that the observed divergence is NOT a function of the instrument's on/off state -- an instrument-caused wire difference would need to correlate WITH instrument state, and it does not here.
_honest_result.diagnosed_root_cause: Real CDP/Playwright-driven synthetic-pointer timing jitter interacting with the shell's own real 120ms pan/zoom debounce (VIEWPORT_QUERY_MIN_INTERVAL_MS, viewportStreamManager.ts) -- a `page.mouse.move(..., {steps:10})` interpolated drag can, under real wall-clock scheduling variance, let an intermediate view-state settle for >=120ms mid-drag, firing an EXTRA, premature debounced viewport_query before the drag's own final resting position is reached. Confirmed in on#1's own sequence: an intermediate viewport_query (bbox xmin=4143d5c8...) sits numerically BETWEEN the previous confirmed query's bbox (xmin=4143c9e0...) and the final, shared-by-all-runs bbox (xmin=4143e58a...) -- exactly the shape of a mid-drag settle.
_honest_result.fixes_already_applied_this_piece_before_: A real, self-inflicted bug (S1's own clamp-check splitting a long pan into SEPARATE mousedown/mouseup drag legs, each risking an independent premature settle) was found and fixed to a single continuous mousedown -> multiple move legs -> single mouseup (residency-harness.mjs's own clampedPanDrag doc comment has the full account); a fixed-sleep settle wait was replaced with the real M6 quiescence+in-flight check; a one-time 'first synthetic gesture of a fresh session' warm-up effect was found and absorbed by an unmeasured warm-up run before the four measured runs. These reduced, but did not eliminate, the residual CDP-timing jitter documented here.
_honest_result.not_fixed_in_this_piece: Eliminating the residual jitter entirely would mean either reducing/removing Playwright's own move-interpolation (steps:10) or otherwise changing how this harness drives the REAL, unmodified production debounce path -- out of this piece's own scope/time budget (the deliberate design choice, this file's own top comment, is to drive the EXACT SAME code path a real operator's drag would, not a parallel test-only seam).
